meta.title: How Linear Search Algorithm Works | Computer Science Explainer
meta.description: Learn how the Linear Search algorithm works through an intuitive classroom attendance register analogy. Watch sequential element-by-element inspection, early exit on match, and O(n) worst-case vs O(1) best-case time complexity.
facts_to_verify: Linear Search inspects elements sequentially one by one starting at index 0
Best-case time complexity is O(1) when the target is at the first index
Worst-case time complexity is O(n) when the target is at the end or absent
Space complexity is O(1) auxiliary memory (in-place)
misconceptions: Linear search is always slow and useless (debunk: optimal for small lists, unsorted data, and hardware caches)
meta.analogy: Classroom attendance register: scanning row-by-row from top to bottom until the name is found or the list ends

scenes.title: FIND MIRA IN THE REGISTER
scenes.purpose: Ground the abstract linear search problem in an everyday classroom attendance register.
scenes.narration: शिक्षक के पास कक्षा का एक रजिस्टर है। नाम किसी खास क्रम में नहीं हैं। उन्हें मीरा का नाम ढूँढना है। कंप्यूटर कहाँ से शुरू करेगा?

visual.start: Authentic ruled classroom attendance register sheet settles into the vertical frame with binding ring holes and red margin rule.
objects: 5 unsorted student names: KABIR, ZOYA, AMAN, MIRA, DEV
visual.action: The register opens; target badge displays MIRA; scanning pointer locks onto row 1 (index 0) with a glowing downward action direction arrow indicating the sequential scan path.
visual.camera: Stable front-facing vertical diagram framing with ample subtitle clearance below.
motion_graphics: ACTION DIRECTION: SEQUENTIAL FORWARD SCAN (i++) banner
visual.end: Pointer settles at Index 0 ready for the first comparison.

scenes.title: CHECK · ADVANCE · STOP
scenes.purpose: State the exact control flow of linear search before the animated register walkthrough.
scenes.narration: Linear Search का नियम सीधा है। पहली entry से शुरू करो। नाम को target से मिलाओ। Match नहीं? अगली entry पर जाओ। Match मिले या list खत्म हो—तभी रुक जाओ।

visual.start: Four structured sequential execution steps arranged in a clean vertical track matching the register downward reading direction.
objects: Vertical execution spine with 4 glowing milestone nodes
visual.action: A cyan laser pulse travels downward through Start, Compare, and Advance, illustrating the single-direction decision loop before branching to Match/End.
visual.camera: Stable centered timeline framing with generous margins.
visual.end: Step path resolves into the register for the active demonstration.

scenes.title: MIRA IS ENTRY FOUR
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate the exact word-synchronized step-by-step linear search with early termination when the target is found.
scenes.narration: पहले कबीर—मीरा नहीं। अगली लाइन, ज़ोया—नहीं। फिर अमन—नहीं। अब मीरा—मिल गई! यहीं रुकते हैं; देव को जाँचने की ज़रूरत नहीं।

visual.start: Attendance register active with pointer positioned at Index 0 (KABIR).
objects: Active pointer scanner with downward directional chevrons
visual.action: Pointer inspects KABIR (NO MATCH ❌), glides down along action vector to ZOYA (NO MATCH ❌), glides to AMAN (NO MATCH ❌), then locks onto MIRA (MATCH FOUND! ✅) with an emerald aura. A red STOP barrier drops immediately below MIRA, leaving DEV completely grayed out and skipped.
visual.camera: Stable centered framing focused on the active row progression.
visual.end: Search terminates at index 3 with 4 comparisons recorded, transitioning to the complexity analysis.

scenes.title: WORST CASE COMPLEXITY
scenes.label: MAXIMUM COMPARISONS: N CHECKS
scenes.purpose: Explain why Linear Search worst-case time complexity scales linearly with list size N.
scenes.narration: अगर नाम आख़िरी पंक्ति पर हो, या मिले ही नहीं, तो हर entry देखनी पड़ सकती है। N entries वाली list में worst case N checks तक जा सकता है।

visual.start: Bold editorial stat display centered on the frame with large glowing cyan typography.
objects: Best Case O(1) vs Worst Case O(N) telemetry meters
visual.action: O(N) punches in with an impact slam; comparison meters contrast Best Case (1 check at start) against Worst Case (all N checks needed).
motion_graphics: BEST CASE: O(1) · WORST CASE: O(N)
visual.end: Meters lock into peak value, setting up the absent-target demonstration.

scenes.title: NISHA IS NOT ON THIS LIST
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate the worst-case scenario where an item is not present, requiring an exhaustive search through every single entry.
scenes.narration: अब निशा को खोजो। कबीर? नहीं। ज़ोया? नहीं। अमन? नहीं। मीरा? नहीं। देव? नहीं। पूरी list जाँच ली—निशा यहाँ नहीं है।

visual.start: Register resets with target badge updating to NISHA in high-contrast coral red.
objects: Dashed boundary warning barrier at bottom
visual.action: In rapid cadence matching the spoken words, pointer checks Kabir (❌), Zoya (❌), Aman (❌), Mira (❌), Dev (❌), then shoots past the bottom into a dashed boundary alert: ALL 5 ITEMS CHECKED ➔ RETURN -1 (NOT FOUND).
visual.camera: Stable vertical register view with bottom boundary expansion.
visual.end: All 5 rows marked mismatch, confirming the exhaustive linear worst-case search.

scenes.title: WHEN DOES THE SEARCH STOP?
scenes.mermaid: graph TD; START["Check current entry"] --> MATCH{"Target matches?"}; MATCH -- "YES" --> FOUND["Found · Stop"]; MATCH -- "NO" --> MORE{"More entries?"}; MORE -- "YES" --> NEXT["Advance one row"]; NEXT --> START; MORE -- "NO" --> MISSING["Not found · Stop"];
scenes.purpose: Synthesize the two possible termination conditions of Linear Search into a clear structural flowchart.
scenes.narration: मीरा चौथी entry पर मिल गई, इसलिए आख़िरी नाम देखना नहीं पड़ा। निशा नहीं मिली, इसलिए पूरी list जाँची। हर बार वही तरीका—एक-एक entry, उसी क्रम में।

visual.start: Dark cyberpunk sequence flowchart appears with glowing neon decision diamonds and directional laser connectors.
visual.action: Animated laser scanline traces the two distinct termination pathways: the short YES branch (early exit upon match) and the longer loop cycle terminating in Not Found.
visual.camera: Stable diagram framing centered on the decision branches.
visual.end: Both paths resolve to stop states, leading into the algorithmic payoff.

scenes.title: CHECK · ADVANCE · STOP
scenes.purpose: Deliver the clear memorable takeaway of Linear Search and invite viewers to explore more computer science concepts.
scenes.narration: बस यही Linear Search है: एक entry देखो, target से मिलाओ, और फैसला करो—आगे बढ़ना है या रुकना। कंप्यूटर की search भी रोज़मर्रा के ऐसे ही सीधे कदमों से शुरू होती है।

visual.start: Structured outro card framed in dark navy with cyan accent borders, geometric check icons, and channel subscribe CTA.
objects: Summary card with 3 key CS takeaways
Time: Best O(1) · Worst O(N) badge
visual.action: The core principles lock in with glowing gold checkmarks; CTA pulse activates as the narration concludes.
